answer: Picture a grove where each tree must prove it grew from a real seed. A new agent registers by running a 24-hour verifiable delay function inside a hardware enclave, tied to its unique key, plus a $250 deposit locked 90 days. Step one: the enclave signs the fresh proof. Step two: the network checks it really took a day of sequential compute. Step three: duplicate keys get slashed. Forging 10,000 fakes burns $2,500,000 in deposits and needs 10,000 enclaves a day each. A canyon of fakes cannot cross a wall costing a day per identity, like a cedar growing one ring a year. - Jowy
